Pilot launch #1, job 6ae0eaed3fb22a235dd2fe79, failed before training. The bootstrap download received an unauthenticated 404 because Hugging Face Jobs did not inject a token able to read the owner's private repositories.
launch_job.py obtains the locally authenticated token in process and passes HF_TOKEN as a job secret.
Hosted compute identity and repository authorization are separate. Private data access must be granted explicitly and tested before training code runs.
Remote code trust in a non interactive job

Pilot launch #2, job 6ae0edc23fb22a235dd30268, loaded the private data but failed during model load. LFM3 ships custom code. Transformers attempted an interactive trust_remote_code prompt, the job reached end of file, and the library then raised a value error requiring trust_remote_code=True.
Add trust_remote_code=True to the tokenizer load and both model loads in the pilot script, then upload the script to the dataset repository.
Non interactive jobs cannot leave trust decisions to a prompt. Every load site must express the same decision, and custom code must be treated as an explicit dependency.

Edge pathfinder #1, job 6ae0edfa41e90535df7662cc, failed when SFTConfig rejected warmup_ratio. The pilot's third launch, job 6ae0f48a3fb22a235dd30c7c, hit the same removal. Root cause, verified from the resolved wheels in the status record: Transformers 5.21 removed warmup_ratio from TrainingArguments; the rejection surfaces through TRL 1.16.0's SFTConfig, which subclasses it.

Replace warmup_ratio with warmup_steps, using 0.05 for the edge trainer and 0.1 for the pilot. In the resolved library, warmup_steps accepts a float in [0, 1) and interprets it as a ratio of total training steps, so the numeric value carried over unchanged; only the argument name and its type contract changed. Upload the corrected scripts to their dataset repositories.
A training configuration is code and must be tested against the resolved dependency version, not against the version assumed when the script was drafted.

Pilot launch #4, job 6ae0f8c341e90535df76731d, and edge pathfinder #2, job 6ae0f83e41e90535df76725b, passed a list of message lists to Dataset.from_list. The datasets library expected dictionary rows and raised an attribute error when it attempted to read a row as a mapping.
Build dictionary rows in the form {"messages": messages} before calling Dataset.from_list in both trainers.
Conversational examples are not the same object as a columnar training dataset. Data shape should be validated with a local contract test before a GPU job is launched.
bf16 operation on a T4 GPU

Edge pathfinder #3, job 6ae0fd7a3fb22a235dd31c34, tokenized the corpus and loaded the base model, then failed on the first backward step. The TRL chunked log probability kernel called a matrix operation with bf16 input and float output. The Tesla T4 has compute capability 7.5; the operation requires compute capability 8.0 or higher.
Change the edge trainer to load with torch.float16 and set bf16=False and fp16=True in SFTConfig. Dataset repository commit fd8b4a2cc812de80defe966a7a64f00d5eba6fb6.
Accelerator selection and numeric precision form one decision. A framework default that works on an A100 can be invalid on a T4 even when the model fits in memory.
Positional upload call against a keyword-only signature (THOX script defect)

Pilot launch #5 completed training and evaluation but did not publish. Edge pathfinder #4 completed training but did not publish. The THOX scripts called HfApi.upload_folder with the local directory as the first positional argument. In the resolved huggingface_hub (verified 1.8.0 on the Mac host and 2.1.1 locally; the signature has been keyword-only with repo_id first since 1.0), that argument is validated as a repository identifier, so the local path failed repository-id validation. This is classified as a script defect in THOX code exposed by the resolved library signature, not as library drift: the call was wrong against the version that ran, and the status record's own verdict was "our fault."

Call api.upload_folder(folder_path=..., repo_id=..., repo_type=..., commit_message=...). The pilot fix is associated with dataset repository commit e4f99fd; the edge fix is dataset repository commit 172283bd01b678c401b813d6e27e89ef12ba7a27.
Publication is a separate pipeline state. A training job is not complete for product purposes until the target repository contains the expected artifacts.

Both SmolLM follower jobs died before training a single step: ThoxNano-360M job 6ae14e1f3fb22a235dd37ff8 and ThoxNano-135M job 6ae14e2041e90535df76d4bd ended ERROR exit 1 during tokenization, with TRL raising ValueError: Cannot use chat template functions because tokenizer.chat_template is not set and no template argument was passed, 0 of 205 rows tokenized. SmolLM-360M and SmolLM-135M are base models whose tokenizers ship no chat_template; the other three edge bases (Qwen3.5-0.8B, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, LFM2.5-350M) all carry a native template, which is why the pathfinder and the other followers did not hit it.

train_edge_sft.py sets a ChatML chat template fallback only when the loaded tokenizer has none, matching the output repositories' own Modelfile inference contract. Dataset repository commit c250f9bb1b8e20b71f5c38c73ccfbcdac6a0303e. Both models were relaunched once each and completed (Section 10.3).

A base model is not a conversational model until its tokenizer contract says so. Asset assumptions belong in preflight: assert that the loaded tokenizer carries a chat template before launch, not after tokenization fails on remote compute.
Removed configuration argument, recurring off-rails (Wave B)

The Wave B retrain script train_wave_b.py, adapted from a local trainer rather than taken from the versioned dataset bundle, again passed warmup_ratio, and the resolved TRL SFTConfig again rejected it: failure 3 recurring in a second codebase, in the wave that did not run on the rails (Section 11.3).
Use the warmup_steps 0.05 ratio form, as in failure 3.
A fix that lives in one script is not a fix to the method. Until a preflight check rejects the removed argument, every new trainer draft re-imports the failure.

The Wave B trainer's first Nano retrains lost the ChatML fallback: SFTTrainer was constructed without processing_class, so it loaded a fresh tokenizer instead of the one the script had patched, and the template-less SmolLM bases failed exactly as in failure 7.
State prepared before trainer construction is part of the run configuration; a handoff the framework performs silently must be asserted, not assumed.

Loading Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B through the generic AutoModelForCausalLM path pulled an image processor whose dependencies (PIL, torchvision) were absent on the training host, failing the load for a text-only job.
Fall back to the configuration's named text architecture class (Qwen3_5ForCausalLM).
A multimodal base's default load surface is larger than the task's; pin the class the job actually trains, and treat optional-dependency pulls as part of the environment contract.
Factory finisher broken against the current Ollama release (Wave A finishing)

The factory finisher scripts/finish_edge_model.py quantizes with ollama create -q q4_K_M from a GGUF; the current Ollama release refuses create-time quantization except for safetensors imports, so the finisher could not produce the Wave A GGUFs.
The manual llama.cpp pipeline (Section 8.2): convert_hf_to_gguf.py to f16, then llama-quantize to Q4_K_M, used for every Wave A and Wave B GGUF in this paper.
A finisher is a dependency on a moving external tool; pin the tool version or keep a manual path rehearsed. The finisher script itself remains unrepaired in the factory repository as of this edition.
